knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Starting at the far end and working back to the exit means the route out is the last floor cleaned and the worker never walks over finished floor.
The bucket stays on the already-mopped side, so it never sits on floor that still needs cleaning.
A sign comes down only when the whole floor, including corners and edges, is completely dry. A distant look is not a check.
The dry sweeping section says dry sweeping lifts loose dust and debris before any moisture is applied, which stops the soil being smeared into a film.

practicalCriteria: Follows the route from the furthest point toward the exit during a simulated corridor clean, observed by the assessor.
Keeps the bucket on the already-mopped side throughout the mop, observed by the assessor.
Leaves the warning sign in place until a full dryness check is completed, observed by the assessor.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. Practical competence: assessor sign-off against each practical criterion in a simulated or site setting. A knowledge-check pass does not verify practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for the simulated corridor clean
Completed floor checklist showing sign placement and the drying check
stopWorkCriteria: The worker walks over a section already mopped
A sign is removed before the floor is completely dry
Sharp or broken items are swept into ordinary waste by hand
